definition: the label I have carried for stepping back, and how far its reading has moved

settled:
I call myself a serial quitter, and the reflex reads that as proof of failure.

I often take solace in not trying for a while, in giving up to give myself time to rest.

The affordability rule reads it the other way. Stepping back is declining what I cannot afford, at the scale of a whole pursuit rather than a single task, and it scores as correctly declined.

That reading is not installed yet. For forty years I held a deeper version of the belief: not only is perfection safe, it is the best I can do.

Acceptance that trying is still flawed and that this is all right lands on me as something to aim at rather than somewhere I have arrived. It does not feel safe yet.

So the old verdict has lost its authority without the new ground feeling safe to be on. That gap is the clearest reading I have of how far there is still to go.
